title: Design System: Rajarshi Lahiri — Digital Garden

display.purpose: The name in the soil band and page h1s. Literata at opsz 72.

title.purpose: List item titles, entry links, role headings.

body.purpose: Long-form prose, capped at 68ch, Literata at opsz 14.

ui.purpose: Summaries, list descriptions, buttons, footer links. Archivo.

label.purpose: Meta rows, tags, filters, nav links, axis ticks, captions. Sentence case, never tracked out.

code.purpose: Inline code and shiki blocks only. Three sites in the whole build; never a voice.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The build declares no box-shadow at all beyond one box-shadow: none reset on a third-party embed. Depth is tonal: soil inset into ground, surface above it, surface-hi on hover.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every colour, border and background transition (0.18s–0.3s).

motion.name: dither-fade
motion.purpose: Cross-fade from the source photograph to the painted dither canvas.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: IntersectionObserver reveal on [data-reveal]; skipped under reduced motion.

components.name: Dithered Portrait Frame
components.description: The one place the material appears. Canvas backing store is sized in dots (cssPx / --dither-cell), so one dot is 3 CSS pixels on every screen regardless of DPR.
components.css: .ds-portrait { position: relative; width: clamp(170px, 22vw, 240px); aspect-ratio: 1; border: 1px solid #2f3d33; border-radius: 8px; background: #080c0a; overflow: hidden; } .ds-portrait::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; border: 1px solid rgba(194,217,164,0.16); border-radius: inherit; pointer-events: none; z-index: 1; } .ds-dither { position: relative; display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; } .ds-dither > img, .ds-dither > canvas { width: 100%; height: 100%; display: block; object-fit: cover; } .ds-dither > canvas { position: absolute; inset: 0; image-rendering: pixelated; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-dither.is-ready > canvas { opacity: 1; } .ds-dither.is-ready > img { opacity: 0; }

narrative.overview:
The site is a plot of ground rendered under a fixed ink budget. Everything sits on a green-black ground (#0d1310), with a near-black soil (#080c0a) held back for the two places something is inset into that ground — the portrait frame and code blocks; the only material in the world is an ordered dither, and it appears exclusively where a real photograph is being reproduced. Dithering is a reproduction technique, not a texture: it earns its place because the five-ink ramp genuinely cannot hold the tones of a photograph, and it is therefore forbidden as wallpaper. The stylesheet contains zero radial-gradient declarations and the build ships no procedural dot field, no animated noise, no grain overlay. That absence is a rule, not an oversight.

Density is editorial rather than dashboard-like. Structure is carried by hairlines (#202a23, #2f3d33) and by whitespace; there are no bordered card grids and no drop shadows anywhere in the build. Confidence is the one thing the interface visualises: a three-step stem ramp encodes how tended a note is, and it is the only place saturation is allowed to mean something. One warm ochre (#d9a441) exists solely as the focus ring — it never appears as decoration.

Confirmed rejections, all verifiable in the built code: no eyebrow or kicker above any heading (the entry kind moved into the meta row), no mono-caps "technical" label kit, no text-transform: uppercase and no positive letter-spacing anywhere sitewide, no decorative section numbering.
keyCharacteristics: One dithered material, applied only to reproduced photographs
Five-ink ramp defined once in CSS and read at runtime by the renderer
Two families only: Literata reads and displays, Archivo runs the interface
Hairlines and whitespace instead of cards and shadows
Growth stage as the single encoded signal, carried by saturation not hue
One warm accent reserved entirely for focus

rules.name: The One Warm Rule
rules.body: Signal ochre appears only as a focus ring. If a new surface needs a warm accent for anything else, it does not get one.

rules.name: The Ramp Is Defined Once Rule
rules.body: --ink-0 … --ink-4 and --dither-cell live in :root and are read from computed style by the dither engine. Never hardcode ink values in a script or a component; changing the CSS custom property is the supported way to change every rendered image.

rules.name: The Saturation-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: Growth stage is encoded by moving along one green from muted to bright. Do not add a second hue to represent state.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Content titles and long-form reading take Literata; interface, meta and micro-labels take Archivo. There is no third voice. The mono stack is for code, not for looking technical.

rules.name: The One Ladder Rule
rules.body: Sizes come from the 1.25 ratio ladder (--t-xs 0.8rem through --t-3xl 3.052rem) off a 16px base. --t-read (1.125rem) is not a rung: it is the serif's optical match to --t-base, used only for serif reading.

rules.name: The No Tracking-Out Rule
rules.body: Exactly one tracking value exists (-0.02em) and it applies only above --t-lg. Zero text-transform: uppercase and zero positive letter-spacing declarations remain sitewide; keep it that way.

rules.name: The Optical Size Rule
rules.body: Literata is variable on opsz 7..72. Set it explicitly per role — small in prose (14), large in display (72). Values above 72 silently clamp, so do not request them.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Hover never lifts, scales a surface, or casts. It changes tone (surface -> surface-hi) or washes with accent-deep at 0.09 opacity. The one scale transform in the build is on a photograph inside a fixed frame, where nothing moves but the image.

rules.name: The Shared Hero Rule
rules.body: There is one hero grid and it lives in the global stylesheet. A page that needs a hero uses .hero-grid as written; it does not re-declare the columns, the gap, or the collapse locally.

dos: Do dither only real photographs, through img[data-dither], and let public/js/dither.js read --ink-* and --dither-cell from :root.
Do encode growth stage with the three-step stem ramp — the .entry-stem rail or the .stage meter — and always pair the visual ramp with text a screen reader can reach.
Do draw structure with 1px hairlines (line, line-hi) and whitespace.
Do keep prose at 68ch and secondary copy between 54ch and 62ch.
Do set font-variation-settings: 'opsz' explicitly per role: 14 for prose, 40–48 for titles, 72 for display.
Do reserve signal ochre for the focus ring, and keep a visible focus ring on every interactive element.
Do put a new collection of things into .work / .work-item, and a staged or dated index into .index / .entry, rather than inventing another list style.
Do use the shared .hero-grid as written for any new hero, portrait included.
Do use authored inline SVG on the 1.5 stroke weight via .icon for any new icon.
donts: Don't use dither, dot fields, grain or noise as a background texture. Zero radial-gradient declarations exist in the stylesheet; keep the count at zero.
Don't put an eyebrow, kicker or overline above a heading. Kind, stage and date belong in the meta row beneath the title.
Don't add a drop shadow, glow, or spread ring. The build declares no box-shadow; depth is tonal.
Don't introduce text-transform: uppercase or any positive letter-spacing. Both counts are zero sitewide.
Don't use monospace as a voice. It is for code, and there are exactly three code sites.
Don't add a third font family or a second tracking value.
Don't build a bordered card grid; the content list replaced it.
Don't number sections decoratively, or add a second hue to signal state.
Don't ship a glyph icon font. Icons are authored inline SVG.
Don't request a Literata opsz above 72; it clamps silently.
